questions.question: What is the primary distinguishing feature of a 'loitering munition' in drone technology?

options.text: It can carry exceptionally heavy payloads for strategic bombing.
options.explanation: This describes strategic bombers, not loitering munitions.

options.text: It is designed for long-endurance, high-altitude surveillance missions.
options.explanation: This describes surveillance drones, not loitering munitions.

options.text: It integrates a warhead and can autonomously search for and strike targets after patrolling an area.
options.explanation: This is the defining feature of loitering munitions.

options.text: It relies solely on satellite communication for beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS) control.
options.explanation: Loitering munitions often use autonomous or pre-programmed control, not solely satellite communication.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered a foundational principle of the World Trade Organization (WTO) that aims to prevent discrimination among trading partners?

options.explanation: Unilateral trade preferences are granted by one country to another without reciprocity, which is not a foundational WTO principle.
Quantitative restrictions refer to limits on the quantity of imports or exports, which are not a foundational principle of the WTO.
MFN is a core principle of the WTO that prevents discrimination among trading partners by ensuring equal treatment.
Bilateral reciprocity involves agreements between two countries to reduce trade barriers mutually, but it is not a foundational WTO principle.

questions.explanation: The Most-Favoured-Nation (MFN) Treatment principle, enshrined in GATT Article I, mandates that any advantage, favour, privilege, or immunity granted by a WTO member to any product originating in or destined for any other country must be accorded immediately and unconditionally to all other WTO members.
questions.hint: This principle ensures that trade benefits are extended equally to all WTO members.

questions.question: Which one of the following principles is a fundamental pillar of the World Trade Organization (WTO) framework, ensuring non-discrimination among trading partners by requiring that a country must treat all other WTO members equally?

options.explanation: Reciprocity is a negotiating principle where countries exchange trade concessions of roughly equal value, not a non-discrimination rule.
The MFN principle is the cornerstone of the WTO, ensuring non-discrimination by requiring equal treatment for all WTO members.
The National Treatment Principle applies to domestic vs. imported goods *after* they have entered the market, not to initial trade advantages.
The WTO prohibits preferential treatment among members, as it contradicts the MFN principle.

questions.explanation: The Most-Favoured-Nation (MFN) principle, enshrined in Article I of GATT, is a cornerstone of the WTO. It mandates that any advantage, favour, privilege, or immunity granted by a WTO member to any product originating in or destined for any other country shall be accorded immediately and unconditionally to the like product originating in or destined for the territories of all other WTO members. This ensures non-discrimination among trading partners. The National Treatment Principle (C) applies to domestic vs. imported goods *after* they have entered the market, while Reciprocity (A) is a negotiating principle, not a fundamental non-discrimination rule of the system itself.
questions.hint: This principle ensures that all WTO members receive the same trade advantages as the most favored nation.

questions.explanation: The 'Peace Clause' (officially known as the Bali Peace Clause, extended in Nairobi) provides temporary protection to developing countries from challenges at the WTO if they exceed their Aggregate Measurement of Support (AMS) limits due to public stockholding programs for food security purposes.
